title: Extension of scalars preserves $\Dctf$
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let
$\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be one of the coefficient maps listed in the blueprint unit
sk-prop-scalar-six, where $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite and $\mathcal O_E$ is
its ring of integers: a homomorphism $A\to B$ of finite admissible rings;
$\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_F$ or $E\to F$ for a finite extension $F/E$ inside
$\Qlb$; $\mathcal O_E\to E$; $E\to\Qlb$; a continuous map
$\mathcal O_E\to A$ to a finite admissible ring; or a composite of these.
The topological coefficient rings are regarded as condensed rings
[sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], finite rings as discrete
ones, and $K_{\Lambda'}=\Lambda'_X\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_X}K$ is
[sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]. Use bounded constructible complexes of finite
Tor amplitude on the small pro-étale site [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude].
Let $X$ be a standing scheme. Then:

1. Every object of $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ is obtained by finitely many shifts,
   extensions and direct summands from objects $a_!P$, where
   $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$ is a locally closed immersion and $P$ is pro-étale locally on
   $S$ of the form $P_0\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}\Lambda_S$ for a bounded complex $P_0$ of
   finite projective $\Lambda(*)$-modules ("locally perfect").
2. For every locally closed immersion $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$ and every
   $P\in D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, if $P$ is locally perfect over $\Lambda$, then $P_{\Lambda'}$ is locally perfect over
   $\Lambda'$, and $a_!(P_{\Lambda'})\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda')$.
3. $K\mapsto K_{\Lambda'}$ maps $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(X,\Lambda')$.

Here finite projective means finitely generated and projective
[def-weil-finitely-generated-module, def-weil-pbc-projective-module]; thus the
local complexes in (1) are perfect scalar-ring complexes [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex].
Tensor with the scalar ring means tensor with its constant sheaf, as in
[det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. For $a=i\circ u$, with $u$ open into
the closure of $S$ and $i$ closed into $X$, $a_!$ denotes $i_*u_!$, using
[sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek, sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Here $i_*=\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_i}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(i^{\Ab}_*)$ is the module pushforward: the underlying sheaf of $i_*M$ is $i^{\Ab}_*M$ and the coefficient action is restricted along $\eta_i$, as in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback].

proof.text: Induct on the listed-map derivation. Each primitive source and target is admissible; finite rings satisfy the annihilation condition by multiplication by ell^n, compositions retain the outside endpoints, and isomorphisms compose their native-presentation witnesses. Apply [lem-sfb-scalar-six-finite-generation] in the finite source case and [lem-sfb-scalar-six-nonfinite-generation] in every integral or field source case. This yields clause (1).

Unpack the specified local cover and choose its scalar complexes. Apply [lem-sfb-perfect-scalar-change-model] to obtain the changed bounded finite-projective scalar complexes and the two chart isomorphisms. Their composite proves local perfectness. Apply [lem-sfb-scalar-six-perfect-extension] to the changed model and the admissible target coefficient. This proves clause (2).

Intersect bounded constructibility thickness from [lem-sfb-scalar-six-admissible-thickness] with finite Tor amplitude thickness from [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. Exact restriction of coefficients is a triangulated functor; its derived left adjoint scalarSixChange receives the adjoint shift structure and is triangulated by Mathlib. Pull the thick target property back along it. A scalar-perfect generator maps, by [lem-sfb-scalar-six-canonical-extension-comparison] and clause (2), into that property. Mathlib shiftClosure_le_iff, extensionProductIter_le_of_isTriangulatedClosed₂ and retractClosure_le_iff give induction on the finite construction from clause (1), proving clause (3). This applies directly to all composites, without a flatness hypothesis.

lean.statement: theorem scalarSixCtf (ell : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime] (k : Type u) [Field k] [Fact (ringChar k).Prime] [Fact (ringChar k ≠ ell)] {Λ Λ' : ScalarSixRing.{u}} (a : Λ ⟶ Λ') (ha : IsListedScalarCoefficientMap ell a) (X : Over (Spec (.of k))) [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom] [IsSeparated X.hom] : (∀ K : ConstantModelConstructibleFiniteTor Λ.X X.left, ∃ n : ℕ, (((sfbPerfectScalarGenerator Λ X).shiftClosure ℤ).extensionProductIter n ).retractClosure K.obj) ∧ (∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (i : S ⟶ X.left) (hi : IsImmersion i) (P : DerivedCategory (ModuleRingedComparison.internalModules Λ.X S)), IsLocallyPerfectScalarModel Λ.X S P → IsLocallyPerfectScalarModel Λ'.X S ((scalarSixChange a S).obj P) ∧ constantModelBoundedConstructible Λ'.X X.left ((sfbLocallyClosedDerivedExtension Λ' i hi).obj ((scalarSixChange a S).obj P)) ∧ DerivedCategory.finiteTorAmplitude _ ((sfbLocallyClosedDerivedExtension Λ' i hi).obj ((scalarSixChange a S).obj P))) ∧ (∀ K : ConstantModelConstructibleFiniteTor Λ.X X.left, constantModelBoundedConstructible Λ'.X X.left ((scalarSixChange a X.left).obj K.obj) ∧ DerivedCategory.finiteTorAmplitude _ ((scalarSixChange a X.left).obj K.obj))
